extraction_notes: Extraction grounded in 60-source leaf covering NL2SQL/NL2VIS interfaces across six research angles: (1) ambiguity resolution (AMBROSIA, AmbiSQL, DataTone benchmarks/systems); (2) semantic parsing foundations (Kamath & Das, Jiasen et al compositionality); (3) pragmatics & user mental models (Gomm et al's cooperative queries, Pirolli & Card information foraging, error analysis papers); (4) interactive disambiguation patterns (clarification questions, widgets, mixed-initiative interaction); (5) HCI foundations (Norman mental models & affordances, Tufte/Shneiderman information viz, Munzner task abstraction); (6) modern LLM-era systems and benchmarks (Text-to-SQL survey 2025, NLI4DB review, test-time compute, multimodal interaction). Concepts extracted at exhaustive depth for leaf scope: 21 concepts covering core tensions in MetroGraph's wedge (ambiguity handling, surface-area reduction, best-of-both UI+NL design, cognitive load minimization, user understanding via transparency). All concepts cite >=1 real source from the leaf's citation pool (60 sources total); coverage includes T0 (latest surveys/reviews), T1 (system papers, benchmarks, empirical studies), and T2 (foundational HCI/viz texts). Gaps acknowledged in sources.json: minimal non-English coverage, sparse accessibility discussion (2 W3C references), limited cost/latency tradeoff analysis for real-time interfaces. Extraction prioritized breadth across research areas + depth on ambiguity/disambiguation (core wedge driver) + pragmatics (user-centered aspect of structured-output design).

concepts.definition: Multi-faceted problem in NL->structured-output where user queries exhibit scope ambiguity (quantifier attachment), syntactic attachment ambiguity, semantic vagueness, and underspecification that multiple valid interpretations coexist.
key_refs: Gomm et al 2025 / Are We Asking the Right Questions
Liu & Li 2025 / Survey Text-to-SQL Era of LLMs
concepts.implication: MetroGraph must distinguish resolvable (cooperative) ambiguities from unresolvable (uncooperative) ones; surface-area bloat worsens this by multiplying ambiguous attribute/edge mappings across mega-schemas.

concepts.definition: System-driven pattern where NL query ambiguities are automatically detected and resolved through targeted clarification questions or interactive widgets, enabling mixed-initiative refinement of intent.
concepts.implication: Core interaction pattern for MetroGraph: replacing AI-chat escape with structured ask-to-clarify loops surfaces user intent incrementally without cognitive overload of showing N alternative interpretations.

concepts.definition: Concrete UI pattern (Sattigeri 2016) for resolving NL visualization ambiguities via embedded, in-context clarification widgets (e.g., dropdowns for column selection, aggregation choice) rather than dialogue or free-form input.
key_refs: Gomm et al 2025 / cooperative query framing
concepts.implication: Direct precedent for MetroGraph's surface-area reduction: widgets constrain to valid schema interpretations, reducing cognitive load vs. free-text correction or agent-chat confusion.

concepts.definition: Application of linguistic pragmatics (Grice's cooperative principle, information scent, cost-benefit reasoning) to NL interface design: understanding user intent through context, shared responsibility for specificity, and minimizing clarification cost.
key_refs: Gomm et al 2025 / shared responsibility in queries
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's wedge: pragmatic interfaces ask users only disambiguating questions whose benefit (resolving ambiguity) clearly outweighs cost (asking), avoiding AI-chat's over-helpfulness that escalates cognitive burden.

concepts.definition: Foundational task of translating NL to formal logical representations (SQL, SPARQL, lambda calculus) executable on structured data; core technical challenge linking NL surface to semantic meaning via compositional decomposition.
key_refs: Kamath & Das 2018 / Survey on Semantic Parsing
KGQA surveys 2024 / semantic parsing for KGs
concepts.implication: Grounding concept: NL ambiguity arises at the mapping layer; MetroGraph's structured output reduces this by making the semantic path (from NL intent to query components) transparent.

concepts.definition: Principle that complex query meaning is built compositionally from simpler semantic units (entities, predicates, operators); complex queries decompose into sub-goals with dependencies.
concepts.implication: Suggests MetroGraph's graph metaphor aligns with how users think: query = connected nodes (entities/steps); explicit decomposition surfaces cognitive chunks, reducing working memory load.

concepts.definition: Critical bottleneck in NL2SQL/NL2VIS where user mentions (e.g., 'sales') map to schema elements (table/column names); ambiguity arises when multiple schema elements match a single mention, or mention context is insufficient.
key_refs: Liu et al 2025 / Text-to-SQL survey (model dimension)
concepts.implication: Direct MetroGraph challenge: mega-schemas amplify entity grounding ambiguity; interactive entity selection (widget-based) reduces user cognitive load vs. automatic guessing.

concepts.definition: Cognitive representation users hold of data structure, query semantics, and system behavior; mismatch between user and system mental models is root cause of errors and confusion.
key_refs: Ahsan et al 2024 / Insights into NL Query Errors
Gomm et al 2025 / what users think about NL interfaces
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's best-of-both design: explicit graph visualization aligns system model with user model (showing schema + query structure), reducing gulf of evaluation (user checks if query matches intent).

concepts.definition: Norman's framework: gulf of execution = distance between user intent and system action affordances; gulf of evaluation = gap between system state and user's ability to perceive it and verify correctness.
concepts.implication: MetroGraph narrows both: NL input closes execution gap (natural expression); graph visualization closes evaluation gap (user sees query mapped to schema structure and can verify intent before execution).

concepts.definition: Pirolli & Card framework: users navigate interfaces by following information scent (implicit signals of value/cost), making cost-benefit judgments about exploration vs. abandonment; successful interfaces maintain strong scent.
concepts.implication: For MetroGraph: strong scent = disambiguation questions signal they resolve real ambiguity; weak scent = AI-chat confusion or over-helpfulness causes users to abandon structured input for freetext.

concepts.definition: Cognitive load theory: extraneous (UI complexity), intrinsic (task difficulty), and germane (learning) load determine user comprehension; NL interfaces risk overloading working memory when ambiguity, schema size, or correction loops multiply.
key_refs: Liu et al 2024 / cognitive load measurement in interfaces
concepts.implication: Critical constraint: MetroGraph's widgets reduce extraneous load vs. free-form clarification; progressive refinement (ask one clarifying question at a time) caps intrinsic load.

concepts.definition: Munzner's hierarchical framework for visualization design: what-why-how breakdown separates data characterization (what), user goal abstraction (why), and idiom selection (how); critical for NL2VIS mapping.
key_refs: Liu et al 2024 / generating analytic specs from NL
concepts.implication: For NL2VIS angle of this leaf: mapping NL queries to visualization requires explicit task abstraction; MetroGraph's structured output supports this by making task decomposition (aggregate, filter, compare) visible.

concepts.definition: Foundational principles (Tufte, Shneiderman): minimize chartjunk, maximize data-ink ratio, use visual hierarchy; overview-zoom-filter idiom; direct mapping between data properties and visual encodings.
key_refs: Tufte 2001 / Visual Display of Quantitative Information
concepts.implication: MetroGraph applies these to query/graph visualization: make data model visible (clear encoding of nodes/edges), support rapid overview of schema and queries, enable drill-down without losing context.

concepts.definition: Norman: affordances = inherent possibilities for action; signifiers = perceivable cues that communicate affordances; mismatch (hidden affordance or false signifier) causes errors.
concepts.implication: For MetroGraph: graph nodes/edges afford drag, click, edit; clarification widgets afford selection; NL input affords free typing; strong signifiers (button labels, visual hierarchy) guide without overwhelming.

concepts.definition: Multi-turn QA/dialogue systems maintain context across turns, enabling users to refine queries iteratively; context includes prior queries, resolved ambiguities, and confirmed interpretations.
key_refs: Kasturi et al 2024 / Conversational QA survey
Zheng et al 2025 / Disambiguation in Conversational QA
concepts.implication: MetroGraph benefit: graph visualization maintains context visually; clarification across turns can reference prior elements (e.g., 'did you mean this table from before?'), reducing repetition.

concepts.definition: Recent trend (2024-25) of scaling inference-time reasoning (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, tree search) for complex NL2SQL; trades latency for accuracy on multi-hop queries via explicit planning/decomposition.
key_refs: Lyu et al 2024 / test-time scaling in Text2SQL
Tong et al 2025 / OraPlan SQL planning
Phuong et al 2025 / test-time compute survey
concepts.implication: Complements MetroGraph: system can show reasoning trace (query plan) as interactive graph; user sees decomposition, surfaces ambiguities early (before execution), enables interactive repair.

concepts.definition: Empirical studies (Ahsan 2024, Ahsan 2023 IUI) document how users discover and repair query errors; common errors = schema misunderstanding, operator confusion, underspecified intent; users prefer interactive explanation over trial-and-error.
key_refs: Ahsan et al 2024 / Insights into NL Query Errors
Ahsan et al 2023 / Empirical Study Model Errors (IUI)
Norman 1995 / user errors in query composition
concepts.implication: MetroGraph design: error recovery should surface user misunderstanding (via explanation widgets like SQLucid) rather than re-asking same question; graph visualization makes error location obvious.

concepts.definition: Combining NL input with direct manipulation (drag nodes, click edges, edit fields); users switch modality based on task (NL for initial high-level query, direct manipulation for refinement).
key_refs: Wilkinson et al 2024 / Multimodal Interaction in Visualization
Quda 2020 / NL visual analytics with direct manipulation
nvAgent 2025 / agent workflow with validation loop
concepts.implication: Core MetroGraph pattern: users can issue NL query, see graph result, then drag nodes/edges to refine without re-querying; reduces friction vs. re-typing NL, increases clarity vs. chat interface.

concepts.definition: Pragmatic tension: when users intentionally leave queries vague (cooperative underspecification) for brevity, systems that aggressively infer/guess risk violating user expectations; over-helpfulness escalates to dialogue without resolution.
key_refs: Gomm et al 2025 / shared responsibility & cooperative queries
Grice / maxim of quantity (be informative but not excessive)
concepts.implication: MetroGraph's wedge: ask only for clarification when ambiguity is structural (not resolvable by inference); avoid AI-chat's trap of trying to guess intent and offering multiple options.

concepts.definition: Systems that expose query generation logic (e.g., step-by-step SQL explanation, visual query plans) enable users to verify intent match; reduces erroneous trust and supports error discovery.
key_refs: Zhu et al 2023 / editable step-by-step explanations
Hoque et al 2022 / principles of query visualization
concepts.implication: MetroGraph strength: graph visualization is inherently transparent (user sees query structure); combined with step-by-step annotation, supports user verification without requiring SQL literacy.
